structure.title: Preface
structure.summary: The text is a company letter from Asian Paints (APL/SEC/26/2025-26/13) dated 3rd June 2025, addressed to BSE and NSE, regarding the Integrated Annual Report for FY 2024-25 and the Notice convening the 79th AGM. It references a prior letter about the AGM scheduled for 26th June 2025 via video conference. Enclosed are the AGM Notice and Integrated Annual Report, including the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report, submitted under SEBI Regulation 34(1). The documents are sent electronically to registered email IDs, with physical copies on request, and a weblink/QR code for others. They are also available on the company website and NSDL e-voting site. The letter is signed by R J Jeyamurugan, CFO & Company Secretary. The attached Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 includes the theme 'Bringing joy to people's lives' with sections on elevate, evolve, engrave, color of the year (Cardinal), and a table of contents covering impact creation, transformation, management discussion, statutory reports, ESG performance, awards, ten-year review, financial statements (standalone and consolidated), and annexures (GRI index, TCFD index, assurance report).

structure.title: Asian Paints FY 2024-25 Annual Report Overview
structure.summary: The page introduces Asian Paints as India’s leading paint and décor brand, outlining its FY 2024-25 themes: Elevate (innovative products and holistic décor solutions), Evolve (adapting to trends, technology, and ESG principles), and Engrave (embedding core values for lasting impact). It highlights the Colour of the Year, Cardinal, and its evocative meaning. It also previews the annual report’s contents: Creating Impact (integrated thinking, ESG snapshot, pioneering transformation, company overview, leadership messages, management discussion, value proposition, stakeholder engagement, materiality, innovation, ESG performance review, awards, ten-year review), Statutory Reports, Financial Statements (standalone and consolidated), and Annexures (GRI index, TCFD index, assurance report).

structure.title: About This Report: Scope, Standards, Assurance, Board Responsibility, and ESG
key_items: This report is aligned to the following standards and frameworks
EXTERNAL ASSURANCE; BOARD RESPONSIBILITY STATEMENT; CONTRIBUTION TO UN SDGs
structure.summary: The page details the report's scope for April 1, 2024, to March 31, 2025, covering financial and non-financial performance, with financial data for standalone and consolidated Asian Paints Limited and non-financial data for standalone operations. It lists adherence to statutes, frameworks, guidelines, and standards including the <IR> framework, Companies Act 2013, Ind AS, SEBI Act, Secretarial Standards, NGRBC, GRI Standards 2021, UN SDGs, and TCFD. External assurance is provided by Deloitte Haskins & Sells LLP under SSAE 3000, SAE 3410, ISAE 3000, and ISAE 3410. It covers key concepts like stakeholder engagement, materiality, ESG commitments with Board oversight, and revised targets. A Board responsibility statement affirms report integrity and approval on May 8, 2025. Contribution to UN SDGs, GRI disclosures, and forward-looking statements are addressed, along with report navigation guidance and contact details.

structure.title: REPORT STRUCTURE
structure.summary: The report outlines ESG commitments integrated into business strategy, structured around environmental, social, and governance pillars. The environmental section covers sustainable operations, focusing on energy conservation, water neutrality, product stewardship, and nature positivity, aligned with material topics like climate change and biodiversity. The social section addresses synergizing relationships, including customer celebrations, community ownership, water stewardship, equitable workplaces, and safety, aligned with material topics such as diversity and human rights. Governance emphasizes transparency, ethics, and sustainable supply chain management, aligned with business ethics and anti-corruption. It also details integrated thinking at Asian Paints, covering purpose, values, business segments, material topics, stakeholders, and ESG pillars, along with performance measurement.

structure.title: FY 2024-25 HIGHLIGHTS
structure.summary: The FY 2024-25 highlights cover sustainable financial performance including revenue, EBITDA, free cash flow, RoCE, and environmental metrics like GHG emissions reduction, electricity consumption, renewable electricity share, and water replenishment. It also includes synergizing relationships metrics such as training participants, employee engagement, safety rate, and NPS. Governance aspects include independent directors, board time on strategy, MSCI ESG rating, and committees chaired by independent directors.

structure.title: SUSTAINABLE OPERATIONS ^
structure.summary: The ESG performance snapshot covers environmental sustainability metrics across energy, product stewardship, water, waste, and emissions. It details reductions in electricity consumption, renewable energy use, GHG footprint, renewable raw materials, lead-free paint, CMR substances, water intensity, and replenishment, with baseline, current performance, and 2025/2030 targets. It also includes plastic packaging collection points, recycled plastic use, hazardous and non-hazardous waste reduction, effluent reduction, and Scope 1 & 2 emission intensity, with targets. Reasons for non-fulfilment of 2025 targets are listed, along with footnotes on indicator scope and renewable electricity aspirations.

structure.title: SYNERGISING RELATIONSHIPS
structure.summary: This ESG performance snapshot covers social, workplace safety, and governance metrics. Social aspects include community engagement through St+art sites, Net Promoter Score, training participants, healthcare beneficiaries, water harvesting potential, employee engagement, psychological safety, and wellness scores, with baseline, current performance, and 2025/2030 targets. Workplace safety metrics include Total Recordable Frequency Rate, Total Severity Rate, and Tier-1 process safety incidents, with targets to sustain global benchmarks. Governance targets cover world-class governance, ethics, transparency, quality, accountability, and sustainable supply chain management. It also notes factors for non-fulfilment of 2025 social targets and indicates progress status for governance goals.

structure.title: World’s largest unified architectural colour system
structure.summary: Asian Paints launched Chromacosm, the world's largest unified architectural colour system with 5,300 curated shades, offering precision and control for architects and designers. The launch featured a collaboration with architect Suchi Reddy, who created an immersive walk-through installation inspired by tantric paintings. The text also covers Asian Paints' annual report highlights: the AP Charter's values and purpose, company achievements including being India's #1 paint company and #2 in Asia, global scale with 26 manufacturing facilities and 60+ countries served, and workforce details like 14,000+ employees and 169,000+ retail touchpoints.

structure.title: Living the AP Charter
structure.summary: This text covers Asian Paints' corporate profile: its heritage since 1942, business in colour, décor, design and protection, and commitment to innovation, sustainability, and safety. It details the AP Charter's role as a foundational guide reflecting identity, purpose, values, and decision-making principles, and its expansion to reinforce an inclusive workplace. It lists six core values—standing for each other's success, creative zeal, integrity, audacity, scientific rigor, and customer passion. It presents key metrics: #1 paint company in India, #1 in decorative lighting, #2 in Asia, #8 globally; 26 in-house paint manufacturing facilities, 60+ countries served, 2.29 million KL annual capacity in India; #1 integrated home décor player, #2 in fabric and furnishing; 14,000+ employees, 72 Beautiful Homes stores, 258 scientists, 169,000+ retail touchpoints, and 12.5 million+ website visitors. It also notes alignment with ESG priorities and progress over past years.

structure.title: DECORATIVE
structure.summary: Asian Paints at a Glance: Decorative and Home Décor segment, India’s leading paint and décor company, offers interior/exterior finishes, waterproofing, wood finishes, enamels, adhesives, tools, undercoats, modular kitchens, wardrobes, bath fittings, sanitaryware, lighting, uPVC windows/doors, wall coverings, furniture, fabrics, furnishings, and rugs. Revenue contribution: K 29,545.3 Crores (87.4% share). International segment serves Asia, Middle East, Africa, South Pacific with revenue K 3,066.4 Crores (9.1% share). Industrial segment provides custom-formulated products via PPG Asian Paints (automotive OEM/refinish, general industrial, packaging, marine) and Asian Paints PPG (protective coatings, powder coatings, road markings), contributing K 1,185.7 Crores (3.5% share, excluding PPGAP as associate).

structure.title: PRODUCTS
structure.summary: The text outlines Asian Paints' products and services, covering a comprehensive suite of decorative and industrial paints, wall coverings, waterproofing, adhesives, fabrics, furnishings, rugs, lighting, uPVC windows and doors, bath fittings, sanitaryware, modular kitchens, wardrobes, and mechanised tools. It details paint offerings for interior, exterior, textures, wood, and metal, along with painting aids. New launches include Royale Glitz Reserv, Nilaya Arc, Apex Ultima Suprema Air-O-Clean, SmartCare Infinia, PU Palette Metal, and PU Palette PS Grey, highlighting features like stain repellency, rustic finish, photocatalytic pollution neutralization, crack-bridging waterproofing, and weather-resistant metal coatings.

structure.title: NEW LAUNCHES
structure.summary: The text details new product launches, including Nilaya Wall W.R.A.P., an anti-bacterial, antifungal, water-resistant, zero-VOC paint-film, and the Sabyasachi for Nilaya Paris-Calcutta collection of wallpapers and fabrics. It also covers services: Colour Ideas, Beautiful Homes Painting Service (offering interior/exterior painting, waterproofing, wood solutions with statistics on customers and dealers), Trusted Contractor Service (with contractor statistics), Beautiful Homes Service (end-to-end interior design), and mentions Colour Next and Asian Paints Beautiful Homes Stores. Various performance metrics are included.

structure.title: OUR GLOBAL FOOTPRINT
structure.summary: The text details Asian Paints' global footprint, operating in 14 countries with 26 manufacturing facilities and serving over 60 markets. It highlights international business revenue of ₹3,066.4 Crores, with regional breakdowns for Africa, Asia, Middle East, and South Pacific. It also covers India operations: 169,000+ retail touchpoints, manufacturing locations with installed capacities across decorative coatings, chemicals, industrial coatings, kitchen, bath, and weatherseal segments, plus upcoming facilities. The distribution network is emphasized as the backbone of performance.

structure.title: CHAIRMAN’S LETTER
structure.summary: The Chairman's letter to shareholders covers: the company's adherence to its Charter values; a challenging year with global volatility, protectionism, geopolitical conflicts, and tepid demand in India's coatings sector, leading to revenue decline despite intensified competition; strategic responses including value-driven offerings (Neo Bharat, Sparc) and premium products (Royale Glitz, Nilaya Arc), dealer and applicator engagement, and the integrated home décor vision with 72 Beautiful Homes Stores; ESG commitment with progress against 2025 targets and focus on 2030 ambitions; board changes with Mr. Jigish Choksi stepping down and Mr. Varun Berry and Mr. Ashish Choksi joining; appreciation for employees; and optimism about India's growth and the company's future, emphasizing brand equity, innovation, and value creation.

structure.title: REIMAGINING OUR CANVAS
structure.summary: The MD & CEO's message reviews a challenging 2024-25 for the coatings industry, marked by demand slowdown, downtrading, and heightened competition. It covers the impact on decorative versus industrial coatings, with rural markets performing better. The company's strategic responses include focusing on economy products, B2B projects, and government tie-ups. Industrial coatings showed resilience, with growth in automotive and non-automotive segments. International markets were mixed, leading to an exit from Indonesia. The message highlights brand-building initiatives, distribution expansion to 1.69 lakh+ touchpoints, servicing scale, innovation with 150+ patents and new products, backward integration investments, and home décor expansion including new stores and Nilaya Anthology. Sustainability commitments and a forward-looking approach are also emphasized.

It also addresses ESG integration, internal controls, enterprise risk management, and references human resources. Finally, it provides a financial review with standalone and consolidated results, key ratios, economic value creation data, investor value metrics, dividend policy, and shareholder support mechanisms.

It describes India's modest economic slowdown due to weak urban consumption but rural pickup, falling inflation, and improved consumption outlook. It discusses political elections, US protectionism, geopolitical conflicts, and India's domestic consumption-driven growth, structural reforms, and the coatings market outlook.

nodes.title: Decorative business in India
nodes.summary: The text covers the decorative paints industry in India for FY 2024-25, noting challenges like softer growth and uneven demand, with urban markets under pressure and rural demand resilient. It details the company's focus on bottom-of-the-pyramid offerings, premium and luxury emulsions, waterproofing growth, and wood-finish category leadership. It highlights innovations, limited-edition packaging with augmented reality, colour leadership with 'Cardinal' as Colour of the Year 2025, and channel partnerships. The B2B business section discusses expansion into Factories, Institutions, and Corporates (FIC) and a new Business-to-Government (B2G) team, leveraging technical collaborations and knowledge leadership. It covers product leadership in construction chemicals, participation in landmark projects like Gati-Shakti, and plans to ramp up presence in line with government spending.

nodes.title: Home Décor
nodes.summary: The text covers Asian Paints' home décor initiatives: Beautiful Homes Stores (72 stores across 54 cities) with phygital network, digital platform, influencer campaigns, and premium formats like Beautiful Homes Studio and Signature Store. It discusses Décor Pro's Category Expertise programme, White Teak's decorative lighting business with revenue decline and store expansion, Weatherseal's uPVC and aluminium windows with retail growth, and Furnishings & Wallcoverings including Nilaya W.R.A.P. innovation and Ador brand. Nilaya Anthology, a luxury design destination in Mumbai, is highlighted. Décor and consumer services include Beautiful Homes Solution, interior design services, Trusted Contractor Service, and painting services.

nodes.title: Kitchen
nodes.summary: Sleek International merged with Asian Paints in March 2025, operating in modular kitchens and components. It offers design-to-execution services via 300+ showrooms in 160 cities, and distributes hardware through 100+ distributors to 4,000+ retailers. The modular business grew, with luxury kitchens contributing over 35% value. A new 72,000 sq ft plant in Wada, Maharashtra, was inaugurated, and the Dezigno digital platform launched for design-to-manufacture integration. Last-mile installation was enhanced with 150+ carpenter teams. Products like Guardian cabinets and pre-laminated shades were introduced, and 5,000+ architect sites serviced. The components segment faced muted demand and regulatory uncertainty (anti-dumping duty, BIS), leading to price revisions and increased India sourcing. New products reached 25% of sales. Sleek Select retailing solution rolled out with 100+ counters, and the portfolio expanded to bed fittings and OEM supply.

nodes.title: Bath Fittings and Sanitaryware
nodes.summary: The text covers the Bath Fittings and Sanitaryware business, detailing FY 2024–25 performance with revenues of ₹356 Crores, product launches (Bathsense CANVAS, Canvas Play, 5 Way Neocontrol+ thermostat, EssEss, PuraShield), plumber training, and after-sales service. It then discusses supply chain challenges, the MPX procurement solution, manufacturing excellence (Kaizens, safety initiatives), and expansions at Mysuru and Ankleshwar. Next, it reviews international business across 13 countries in South Asia, Middle East, Africa, and South Pacific, covering operating environments, currency issues, and business performance by region, including Indonesia exit, Middle East store launch, and South Pacific earthquake impact.

nodes.title: Industrial business in India
nodes.summary: The text covers Asian Paints' industrial coatings business in India through two 50:50 joint ventures with PPG Industries: PPG-AP (automotive, industrial, refinish, packaging, and marine coatings) and AP-PPG (non-automotive industrial coatings). It details operating environments and business performance for both JVs, including market trends, government schemes, and growth strategies. It also discusses ESG integration, internal control systems and their adequacy, enterprise risk management, and references to human resources and industrial relations. The document is part of Asian Paints' Integrated Annual Report 2024-25.

structure.title: NILAYA ANTHOLOGY
structure.summary: Asian Paints launched Nilaya Anthology, a 100,000+ sq ft experiential design destination in Mumbai's mill district, positioned as India's first international design destination. It operates on principles of Curation, Creation, and Experience, offering global and Indian design products including carpets, textiles, ceramics, and collaborations with brands like Cassina and Sabyasachi. The umbrella brand spans luxury bathware, furniture, lighting, and more, enhanced by installations and cultural programming. A quote from CEO Amit Syngle emphasizes redefining luxury retail. The text also introduces a value proposition section covering value creation, stakeholder engagement, materiality, and innovation/manufacturing excellence, with page references.

structure.summary: The text covers Asian Paints' innovation and manufacturing excellence, detailing the Alchemy 2025 case study competition with themes like AI for coating design, polymer-nanomaterial hybrids, sustainable architectural coatings, and smart coatings, which drew over 6,800 participants and featured a winning case on plasmonic metals. It also describes performance excellence initiatives, major expansions at Mysuru and Ankleshwar plants, a new white cement facility in Fujairah, and data analytics advancements including self-serving BI solutions and prescriptive analytics. structure.summary: The text outlines Asian Paints' sustainable operations as a key ESG pillar, highlighting FY 2024-25 achievements: 57.6% renewable electricity at decorative plants, 478% water replenishment, and 20,150 tonnes of recycled plastic in packaging. It lists key material topics (climate change, waste, water, end-of-life management, product stewardship, biodiversity, supplier sustainability, technology) and ESG strategy areas (energy conservation, product stewardship, water neutrality, nature positive). Stakeholders impacted include customers, communities, employees, investors, government, and vendors, with UN SDGs referenced. A 2025 reflection notes steady progress since FY 2013-14, acknowledges unmet targets due to lower production, capacity expansion, and regulatory shifts, and details advances in water stewardship, supply chain sustainability via Samaveta, and circularity. Future focus is on scaling successes and embedding environmental responsibility across the value chain toward 2030 goals.

structure.title: SAFE WORKPLACE
structure.summary: Asian Paints' SAFE WORKPLACE section details its global safety benchmarks, ISO 45001 certification, and 2025 targets for TRFR, TSR, and process safety incidents. It covers rigorous OHS systems, smart technologies, automation, and design safety via HAZOP, DCS, and robotic palletizers. Employee safety includes 360-degree guarding, digital incident logging, CAPA, and contractor pre-qualification. Visual safety training and 'Walk the Park' improved engagement. Special 27, an elite emergency response team, received advanced training. Ergonomic innovations include telescopic conveyors, fork-mounted cameras, and ErgoPlus software. Warehouse safety, safety culture, and road safety initiatives are noted. PSM improvements feature IoT, Bowtie risk profiling, and competency training with Suraksha Doots. Case studies cover heat exchanger choking prevention, automation of raw material transfer, and RPM sensors. Safety metrics for FY 2024-25 and FY 2023-24 are compared, and stakeholder engagement includes a Business Partner Code of Conduct and regulatory advocacy. The company achieved the generative stage in the coating industry.

nodes.title: SAFETY AT EVERY STEP
nodes.summary: Asian Paints aims for global safety benchmarks in coatings, using rigorous OHS systems, training, and a culture of accountability. The long-term roadmap emphasizes smart technologies, automation, and safer process designs. All plants are ISO 45001 certified, with 8 decorative paint plants BSC five-star certified. Targets for 2025 include TRFR ≤0.98 (achieved 1.0), TSR ≤150 (achieved 40.7), and Tier-1 process safety incidents ≤3 (achieved 3). Safety is embedded from design via HAZOP studies, DCS automation, dual-level tank controls, pneumatic conveying, and robotic palletizers. Employee safety includes 360-degree guarding, man-vehicle risk assessments, TRFR/TSR guidelines, BSC-aligned standards across 63 parameters, digital incident logging, CAPA, and contractor safety pre-qualification and training.

nodes.title: VISUAL SAFETY TRAINING TO ENHANCE RETENTION THROUGH EXPERIENCE
nodes.summary: The text covers visual safety training to improve retention through experiential learning, including transforming CTPS modules into interactive displays and a 'Walk the Park' concept, which improved engagement and reduced incidents. It then details a safety monitoring mechanism with certified hygienists conducting triennial assessments, regular medical surveillance, air quality monitoring for VOCs and RSPM via accredited labs, ventilation and ergonomic audits, tracking of noise and dust, internal/external audits, SUSA conversations, HARP evaluations, and screening raw materials using IARC and GHS norms, referencing GRI 403-2 and 403-3.

nodes.title: SPECIAL 27: REDEFINING EMERGENCY RESPONSE
nodes.summary: The Mysuru plant formed Special 27, a 27-member cross-functional elite team, to enhance emergency preparedness. Partnering with LCS India, members completed two nine-day trainings on 13 advanced response techniques like tunnel rescue, fire suppression, chemical handling, and confined space entry, using simulations and scenario-based drills. A full-scale mock drill with 40+ external officials showcased their performance, earning acclaim. The team is now integrated into the plant’s emergency response system, symbolizing agility, teamwork, and preparedness. Beyond safety, Special 27 represents a culture shift reflecting the organization’s focus on protecting lives, rapid response, and industrial safety standards, aligned with GRI 403-7.

nodes.title: ERGONOMIC INNOVATION AT THE PUTTY BLOCK
nodes.summary: The text covers ergonomic innovation at the Putty block via a telescopic conveyor system to reduce manual lifting risks, along with safety enhancements and productivity gains. It describes building a safety culture through training, family engagement, competitions, and events. It lists safety initiatives such as road safety videos, contractor safety enhancements, CAPA reviews, unsafe condition corrections, injury-free days, and quarterly theme-based drives. It also outlines Process Safety Management improvements including digital IoT interfaces, training, Bowtie risk profiling, and safety investments. Finally, it notes the company's achievement of generative stage in the coating industry.

Risk management is integrated into planning and operations, with a framework for identifying and mitigating risks, a Risk Management Committee (RMC) chaired by an Independent Director, a Board-approved risk charter and policy, materiality matrix, and ISO 31000 alignment. nodes.title: Asian Paints Risk Management: Approach, Process, and Strategic Integration
nodes.summary: The page outlines Asian Paints' risk management framework as integral to planning and growth, with a culture of risk awareness. The approach is governed by a Board-approved risk charter and policy, with RMC meetings, a materiality matrix, and PESTLE monitoring, aligned with ISO 31000. A five-stage process covers identification, assessment, mitigation, recording, and monitoring, supported by KRIs, impact areas, and VaR methodology. Risk management in strategy setting involves the AP Charter and periodic RMC and Board reviews.

nodes.title: Enterprise Risk Management and Risk Matrix Overview
nodes.summary: The page outlines the Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) process, which manages uncertainty, strengthens governance, meets stakeholder expectations, and enhances resilience for sustainable growth. It lists eight guiding principles: integrated, structured and comprehensive, customised, best available information, continual improvement, human and cultural factors, inclusive, and dynamic and futuristic. It also presents a risk matrix categorizing risks using two axes—endogenous/exogenous and strategic/operational—with four tolerance quadrants, and provides examples of risks in each quadrant, such as people risk, climate risk, regulatory landscape, and cyber security risk.

For each, it provides impact, description, rationale, and mitigation strategies. nodes.title: a) Business combinations
nodes.summary: The text outlines accounting policies for business combinations under Ind AS 103, covering the acquisition method. It details measuring identifiable assets and liabilities at fair value, with exceptions for deferred tax and employee benefits under Ind AS 12 and 19. Contingent liabilities are measured at fair value. Consideration includes contingent consideration, remeasured at fair value with changes in profit or loss. Goodwill arises when consideration exceeds net fair value; bargain purchases yield a gain in other comprehensive income and capital reserve. Transaction costs are expensed, except equity/debt issuance costs. Common control combinations use the pooling of interests method, accounting net assets at carrying amounts, with any excess/shortfall of consideration over share capital recognized as capital reserve.

Recognition and measurement of defined contribution plans:
The Company recognise contribution payable to a defined contribution plan as an expense in the Statement of Profit and Loss when the employees render services. If the contributions payable for services received from employees before the reporting date exceeds the contributions already paid, the deficit payable is recognised as a liability after deducting the contribution already paid. If the contribution already paid exceeds the contribution due for services received before the reporting date, the excess is recognised as an asset to the extent that the prepayment will lead to a reduction in future payments or a cash refund.

structure.title: Note 29 (D) : Capital Management
structure.summary:
Note 29 (D) : Capital Management
For the purpose of the Group’s capital management, capital includes issued capital and all other equity reserves attributable to the equity shareholders of the Group. The primary objective of the Group when managing capital is to safeguard its ability to continue as a going concern and to maintain an optimal capital structure so as to maximize shareholder value.
The capital structure of the Group consists of debt, which includes the borrowings disclosed in Note 15 and equity attributable to owners of the Parent Company, comprising issued capital, reserves and accumulated profits as presented in the Consolidated Statements of Changes in Equity.
Consequent to such capital structure, there are no externally imposed capital requirements. In order to maintain or achieve an optimal capital structure, the Group allocates its capital for distribution as dividend or re-investment into business based on its long term financial plans.
